solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Biased towards small gardens

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London, often just called Kew

explanation.surface: Someone's opinion leans in favour of modest little gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the famous botanic garden in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To skew results is to bias them, so skew as an adjective-like noun matches slanted, prejudiced.

clue.text: Visit old copper and get exhausted

parts.note: to visit someone is to go to see them
d was the symbol for the old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: Calling on an elderly policeman leaves you worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old copper' suggests a retired policeman, but it is the pre-decimal penny, abbreviated d.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that bolts and runs to seed is spent, so the idiom means to deteriorate or become worn out.

clue.text: Daniels' last part, inmate in Scum

indicators.note: the final part of the word Daniels' supplies its closing letter

parts.note: an old lag is a long-serving convict, so lag means an inmate

explanation.surface: A line about Daniels' final role as a prisoner in the borstal film Scum.
explanation.walkthrough: Scum is a 1979 British film about a youth prison, which makes it look like a title rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slag is the dross skimmed off molten metal, and figuratively worthless people, so it means scum.

clue.text: Poem concerning concert hall

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A poem written about a venue for concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece an odeon was a roofed building for musical performances, a concert hall.

clue.text: To pass oneself off as a peer's not out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are jumbled, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive s included as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pretending to be a member of the nobility is improper behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To personate someone is to impersonate them, assuming their identity.

clue.text: Busts some rhymes about a dispute

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to bust rhymes is hip-hop slang for rapping, so the phrase means raps

explanation.surface: A rapper's verses concern an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some rhymes' looks like a hidden-word signal, but the whole phrase is slang for raps.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a brief argument or bout of verbal sparring.

clue.text: Drama with American soldier and a 'Miss' finally served up — with this setting?

definitions.text: Drama with American soldier and a 'Miss' finally served up — with this setting?

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese drama
GI is a US soldier

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word Miss

explanation.surface: Describes the musical Miss Saigon: a drama with an American GI and a 'Miss', asking where it is set.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed string NOGIAS reads upwards. The musical Miss Saigon is set in Vietnam during the war.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical about a GI and a Vietnamese girl takes its setting, and half its title, from this city.

clue.text: Northern bird to draw without specific information

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to kedge is to haul a ship along by a small anchor, so to draw it
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A northern bird sketched without any particular details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside. To kedge is a nautical verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is information known, and the clue frames it as particular facts someone holds.

clue.text: Sally in the Afternoon is a song

indicators.note: in places the name inside the time abbreviation

parts.note: PM (post meridiem) denotes the afternoon
Sal is the short form of the name Sally

explanation.surface: Like a film title, Sally in the Afternoon is called a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, as in the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Very busy person in charge

parts.note: a man is a person
IC is the abbreviation for in charge, as in 2IC

explanation.surface: The boss is run off their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frantic, hectic activity, as in a manic day at work.

clue.text: Having grown up to be immoral

indicators.note: up here means mixed up, so the letters of grown are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who became corrupt as they grew into adulthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grown up' reads as a single phrase, but 'up' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong in its moral sense means wicked or unethical.

clue.text: Decapitated brent goose processed to extract a hormone

indicators.note: processed means worked over and changed, so these letters are rearranged
a head removed means the first letter of brent goes

explanation.surface: A grim kitchen scene: a beheaded goose is processed to obtain a hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decapitated' takes the B off brent, leaving RENT, which with GOOSE is rearranged. A brent goose is a small wild goose.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrogen is the principal female sex hormone, the British spelling of estrogen.

clue.text: Something played by disc jockey only partly remembered …

indicators.note: only part of the word remembered is used: its opening and closing letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A DJ half-recalls a track he played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only partly' drops REM and RED from remembered, leaving EMBE. 'played' suggests a record, but the answer is an instrument, a West African drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A djembe is a goblet-shaped hand drum, so it is a thing that musicians play.

clue.text: Two's company

parts.note: the proverb 'two's company' is read literally: a company made of two performers

explanation.surface: The proverb that two people make good company.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of musicians or performers working together forms a two-person act.

clue.text: Man, for example, making offer to include gym

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction
PE (physical education) is school gym

explanation.surface: A man makes an offer that includes gym membership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but here means humankind as a two-legged creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two legs, so a man is an example of a two-footed animal.

clue.text: … but this may help Minnesota with income redistribution

parts.note: MN is the US postal abbreviation for Minnesota

indicators.note: redistribution means the letters of income are shared out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue: an income redistribution might help Minnesota.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 'partly remembered' in 13 across: this is what helps memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid helps you recall something only partly remembered, as the linked clue says.

clue.text: Keen to find a way of doing things at the ballot box

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a method of operation
a ballot box is sometimes called an urn, from the ancient vessel for votes

explanation.surface: Someone eager to find a new voting procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but is the verb meaning to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in lament for the dead, so it means grieve.

clue.text: Possibly felt opus by Saint-Saëns initially required organ parts

indicators.note: possibly signals that felt opus could be rearranged into something else
initially picks the opening letter of Saint-Saëns

explanation.surface: A composition by Saint-Saëns, perhaps his Organ Symphony, needed certain organ components.
explanation.definitionFit: Flue stops are organ stops controlling pipes that sound like a whistle, without reeds.

clue.text: Oscar possibly lied about dad wanting to keep mum?

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the father
possibly means the letters of lied could be arranged another way

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Someone lied about their father to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep mum' means stay quiet, but here it is literal: possess your mother, as in the Oedipus complex.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freud's theory the Oedipus complex is a son's desire for his mother, so the question-marked phrase fits.

clue.text: Titania initially rejected Bottom's assertion, which is destructive

definitions.note: the clause describes a thing that wreaks destruction, standing for a noun

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Titania
rejected means thrown back, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: Bottom, being a bottom, might claim 'I'm anus': I'M + ANUS

explanation.surface: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Titania dismisses what Bottom the weaver claims.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is Shakespeare's weaver, but here also the rear: his assertion is 'I'm anus', reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal wave from an undersea earthquake devastates coastlines, a hugely destructive thing.

clue.text: Tailed Red Baron flying around Italy, being this?

definitions.text: Tailed Red Baron flying around Italy, being this?

indicators.note: around means surrounding the country's letter
flying suggests letters scattered and rearranged
tailed means its tail is cut off, so the last letter of Red goes

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: The Red Baron, tailed by an enemy plane, flies over Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' means docked of its last letter, and 'flying' rearranges the remainder around I. The Red Baron was the German fighter ace Manfred von Richthofen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flying in a plane is up in the air, the state the clue's scene describes.

clue.text: Frigid and bitchy at intervals

indicators.note: at intervals means every other letter of bitchy is taken

explanation.surface: Someone cold and occasionally spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid and icy both mean extremely cold, and figuratively unfriendly.

clue.text: Requirement to remain outside when deeply involved

indicators.note: the verb for remaining stands outside, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: to keep is to remain, as in keep calm
a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A requirement to stay outdoors when heavily committed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in something up to your knees is figuratively to be heavily engaged or immersed.

clue.text: Letter from Greece international selector, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a selector who awards international caps would be a capper

explanation.surface: A Greek international's selector writes a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cap' is awarded for each appearance for one's country, so the selector is a 'capper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet, corresponding to K.

clue.text: Fifty-fifty ball, all the same

parts.note: evens are betting odds of one to one, a fifty-fifty chance
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A footballer's 50-50 ball, contested regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless or despite that, the same as all the same.

clue.text: Terribly angry about line getting twisted

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled word goes round the line
terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters of angry are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone furious at a queue becomes wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarly describes gnarled, knotty wood, so it means twisted or bent.

clue.text: Prison guard's earnings

definitions.meaning: slang for a prison officer, a warder
slang for wages or salary, as in a decent weekly pay packet

explanation.surface: A warder's pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British slang: a jail warder, and the wages someone is paid.

clue.text: Sounds like new Chelsea player is performing under pressure

indicators.note: sounds like says the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: Nemanja Matić was a Chelsea footballer; 'new Matic' said aloud

explanation.surface: A newly signed Chelsea player performs well under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The P is silent, so 'new Matic' gives the sound. Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumatic machines such as drills work by compressed air, so they operate by air pressure.

clue.text: Shakespearean quits gathering

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's usage, to be even or square with someone
a gathering, as of hounds and riders before a hunt

explanation.surface: A gathering where Shakespeare's characters part company.
explanation.definitionFit: In Much Ado the word means even or quits; a hunt assembly is also so called.

clue.text: Some scaremongering about international banker

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the hidden letters read backwards
some means part of the word scaremongering is used

explanation.surface: Scaremongering about a global financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the gnomes of Zurich' is a nickname for Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss financiers were famously dubbed the gnomes of Zurich, so a gnome is an international banker.

clue.text: Said to have encouraged a French writer

indicators.note: said signals a sound-alike word

parts.note: geed (up) means urged on or encouraged

explanation.surface: A French writer supposedly encouraged others.
explanation.definitionFit: André Gide was a French novelist who won the 1947 Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: Novel from Hammett sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read upwards, so the letters reverse
from means the letters are taken out of inside the name Hammett

explanation.surface: A book from Dashiell Hammett is parodied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like mockery but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's 1815 work is a famous novel.

clue.text: Late reverend stripped part of church, …

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are taken off

parts.note: the late Rev Ian Paisley, Northern Irish preacher and politician

explanation.surface: A deceased clergyman was undressed in part of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley founded the DUP, which the next clue picks up.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage between rows of pews, or a side section of a nave, is part of a church.

clue.text: … DUP's money wasted creating a sort of name

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or messed up, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive s included as a letter

explanation.surface: The Democratic Unionist Party's money squandered on a false identity.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, linked to Paisley in the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name or alias is a kind of fictitious name used instead of one's own.
